newsitem.title: FRANCE: Scientology church hails French leaders' acquittal.
newsitem.headline: Scientology church hails French leaders' acquittal.

text.p: The president of the international Church of Scientology has said a French court acquitted all the movement's national leaders in France in a trial stemming from a follower's suicide in Lyon, central France.

"We are pleased, of course, that the Lyon judges acquitted the national leaders of the Church in France," Heber Jentzsch, president of the Church of Scientology International, said in a statement faxed to Reuters.

He said all the movement's national leaders were among the eight defendants acquitted by the Lyon criminal court last Friday. Fourteen other defendants had been merely "slapped on the wrist" after an eight-day trial, Jentzsch said.
"Only one, the former leader of a local mission in Lyon, was sentenced to jail," he said.
He was referring to former head of the Church of Scientology in Lyon, who was convicted of manslaughter and fraud and sentenced to 18 months in jail plus another 18 months suspended.
Reuters erroneously described Mazier during the trial as former head of the French Church of Scientology.
Jentzsch called the proceedings "a heresy trial" brought on by political pressure and said appeals would be pursued.
At the trial, prosecutors depicted the church as a business masquerading as a religion, whose chief function was to extort cash from the gullible using abusive high-pressure techniques.
Defence lawyers countered that the organisation was a legitimate religion and argued that their clients were the innocent victims of a campaign by the centre-right government to crack down on cults.
